edges.description: Proposed by the discoverers from the clinical overlap with KIF22-related SEMD-JL: both genes act on vesicle transport from the Golgi to the plasma membrane. No study has tested the link in joint tissue.
Same hypothesised shared vesicle-transport mechanism as the dislocation edge; untested.
Hedgehog signal transduction depends on the primary cilium, and the knockdown cells show both defects; the cilium is the presumed link.

The central nervous system findings are attributed to a ciliopathy by the reporting authors on the basis of one affected individual. Nothing links the fibroblast cilium defect to brain development directly.
Same ciliopathy interpretation as the intellectual disability edge.
Same ciliopathy interpretation as the intellectual disability edge.
Both findings come from the same knockdown cells; the source does not show that restoring Hedgehog signalling corrects the differentiation markers.
A cell-line differentiation defect is the closest measured correlate of disordered growth-plate ossification; no growth plate from a patient or animal model has been examined.
Reduced osteogenic differentiation in fibroblasts is suggestive of, but not shown to cause, the ossification defect.

nodes.description: Disordered endochondral ossification is the tissue-level process invoked to explain the progressive skeletal deformity and the epiphyseal, metaphyseal and spinal dysplasia. It is stated in the clinical literature as background rather than demonstrated histologically in SEMDJL3.

nodes.description: During in vitro chondrogenesis of Exoc6b-knockdown ATDC5 cells, Col2a1 is deregulated, Ihh and Col10a1 rise, the hypertrophy brake Axin2 falls, the terminal hypertrophy and matrix-remodelling genes Mmp13 and Adamts4 fall, and Bglap is suppressed. nodes.description: In cell lines EXOC6B promotes basal autophagy through AMPK activation and mTOR inhibition, and this autophagy is what lengthens the primary cilium.
